title: Complete weight-backed full-forward on all 27 layers of a real GGUF

model.note: Every weight tensor is aliased directly from the memory-mapped GGUF payload; nothing is copied or synthesised.

what_runs: Real embedding lookup (token_embd.weight, real Q4_K row dequantised by ggml)
Real RMSNorm on blk.N.attn_norm.weight (ggml_rms_norm + learned weight)
Real MLA: lora_proj (attn_kv_a_mqa) -> kv_a_norm on the lora prefix -> kv_b (real tensor shapes)
Real attention over a real per-layer KV cache (score, softmax, value aggregation)
Real FFN norm then EITHER dense SwiGLU (leading-dense block) OR MoE: router (ffn_gate_inp, F32) -> top-2 experts -> SwiGLU -> weighted sum -> shared expert (shexp)
Real final RMSNorm (output_norm.weight) + real output projection (output.weight)
Real soft_max sampling; the argmax token steers the next embedding row

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: MLA kv split double-counted the rope dimension
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: kRow + vRow came to 4160 while kv_b emits only 4096 rows. The rope dims are already part of kv_b's output (bOut = heads * (qk_nope + rope_per_head + v_head)), so adding them on top overflowed by 64. Fixed by deriving the K/V slices from bOut and heads only.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: all three MoE expert tensors aliased one shared staging buffer
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: aliasExpertRows() resizes its buffer, which frees the previous tensor's data and left gt/ut/dt pointing at the wrong expert. Fixed with three separate buffers.
defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: code review of the expert loop

defects_found_and_fixed.detail: ffn_down.weight takes 10944 elements, not 2048; the 2048-element hidden state was being passed to it. Fixed by threading the 10944-element SwiGLU intermediate through gate -> silu -> up -> down.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: F32 tensors (ffn_gate_inp router) were rejected as unaliased
defects_found_and_fixed.detail: aliasWeight() required type_traits::to_float, but F32 tensors have none because they need no dequantisation. Fixed to accept F32 (a plain copy is the correct dequantisation).

acceptance_gates.token_ids_valid: PASS (0 <= id < the sampled logit count)

what_this_does_not_establish: TPS certification. The 27-layer run took 5.31 s per token (0.19 TPS) because it re-read weights from the memory-mapped file per operation with no GPU residency, no expert caching, no tiling of the activations, and no continuous batching. It is a correctness run, not a performance run.

Reference-correct logits. The logits are finite and in a plausible range, but they have NOT been compared against a reference decoder (e.g. llama.cpp) for numerical parity. Argument-level agreement on architecture alone does not certify output equality.
Coherent text generation. No tokenizer round-trip or chat template was applied, so the token ids have not been rendered as text.
GPU inference. All 27 layers ran on the CPU backend. The Vulkan quant-dot kernel verified in RAWRXD_DEEP2_GPU_QUANT_DOT_002 is not wired into this executor yet.
next_gates: Reference parity: generate logits for a known prompt with this path AND an independent decoder, then compare per-position cosine / relative RMSE and the resulting token ids.
Renderer: drive tools/deep2_universal_ingest's tokenizer so generated ids become text.
GPU residency: wire ExecuteQuantDot into the FFN/projection ops (blueprint step 03) so the 5.31 s/token weight-bandwidth binding is replaced by the Vulkan path.
Expert residency + prefetch: keep hot experts resident (the ffn_down_exps sweep is 74/75 GiB per token).
Only then measure TPS toward the 150 floor.
